scope: Signed-in, account-scoped Explore hide preference and Star profile independence. Local implementation review and migration rehearsal; no production mutation or deployment claimed.
decision: Hide is personalization, not community moderation. Anonymous visitors and developer API keys cannot write a preference. A Star profile remains a complete public gallery even when a viewer hides one of its creations from Explore.

server: One allowlisted mutation helper verifies same-origin/session intent, resolves the authenticated account server-side, rejects anonymous and developer-key callers, and never accepts a caller-supplied viewer identity.
Explore feed reads apply the private preference only for a verified session and use private no-store caching; Star profile reads intentionally skip it.
Hide and undo are idempotent, reversible, and return generic public errors without database or moderation details.
database: Migration 20260920120000 adds forced-RLS private preference and per-account abuse-ledger tables.
The active list is capped at 500; successful new hides use a 30-per-ten-minute and 200-per-day ledger that survives undo; duplicate hides do not consume allowance.
The historical anonymous/global function is execution-revoked and browser roles cannot read or write moderation records.
Migration 20260920123000 explicitly revokes inherited service-role ACLs before granting only the operations required by the private function.
ui: Hide is labeled for the current viewer, sign-in is requested before mutation, optimistic removal has undo, and failed writes restore the card.
Touch targets are at least 44px and the hide affordance is available from keyboard focus as well as pointer hover.
